# AI Voiceover Studio

> AI Voiceover Studio (`ai-voiceover-studio`, command `voiceover`) is an open-source, MIT-licensed Python 3.9+ CLI and library that turns a Markdown script into an AI voiceover (text to speech), SRT subtitles and a captioned faceless video for YouTube, Shorts, Reels and TikTok — B-roll per paragraph with Ken Burns motion, TikTok-style word-by-word captions, an animated hook card and background music ducked under the voice. It works out of the box with free Microsoft Edge neural voices (no account, no API key); OpenAI and Miragea (voice cloning) are optional engines.

Key facts:

- Install: `git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio && pip install -e ".[edge]"`. Needs ffmpeg (with libass) for MP3 and video; `voiceover doctor` checks the setup. Not yet published on PyPI.
- Faceless video: `voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok --music ambient -o out/video.mp4`; vertical Short: add `--vertical`.
- Audio + subtitles only: `voiceover script script.md -o out/` → `voiceover.mp3`, `voiceover.srt`, `manifest.json`. One line: `voiceover say "text" -o out.mp3`.
- Script format: `[SPEAKER]: text` lines, `[pause 1.5]`, `[SPEAKER](tags=a|b, speed=1.1, lang=es): ...`, `![](clip.mp4)` sets the B-roll of the next paragraph, `**bold**` words are highlighted in captions. Each speaker automatically gets its own voice (edge engine); `--lang` sets the language for Latin-script languages other than English.
- Engines: `edge` (free, default without MIRAGEA_API_KEY, 300+ voices / 70+ languages), `miragea` (MIRAGEA_API_KEY; voice cloning from a reference URL, expressive models, subtitle recognition; default when the key is set), `openai` (OPENAI_API_KEY), `dummy` (`--dry-run`, offline). Custom engines via the `VoiceProvider` interface and the `ai_voiceover_studio.providers` entry point.
- Caption styles: `tiktok` (default vertical), `clean` (default landscape), `bold`, `minimal`, `box`. Music: `--music ambient|pulse` (generated at render time, royalty-free) or a file; `--no-duck` disables ducking.
- Agent use: every command supports `--json`; exit codes 0 ok, 1 task failed, 2 usage/API error; agent skill at skills/ai-voiceover/SKILL.md.
- It does not include a timeline editor, stock-footage library, lip-sync or automatic translation.
This file concatenates the project's documentation. Each part starts with its source URL.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio/main/README.md

# AI Voiceover Studio — open-source AI voiceover and faceless video generator
**AI Voiceover Studio** is an open-source Python CLI that works as an AI voiceover tool and faceless YouTube video generator: it turns a plain script into natural text to speech, SRT subtitles and a finished text-to-speech video with TikTok-style word-by-word captions — free voices included, no API key needed.

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok --music ambient -o out/video.mp4
voiceover video --script examples/demo.zh.md --vertical --music ambient -o out/short.mp4
```

That is the whole setup. You get `out/video.mp4` (1080p: B-roll with Ken Burns motion and transitions, an animated hook card, word-by-word captions and music ducked under the voice), `out/video.srt`, and the voiceover track in `out/video_voiceover/`. It needs Python 3.9+ and [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org); `voiceover doctor` checks both. For the exact look of the demo, pass a bold font with `--font` (the demo used the free Montserrat ExtraBold and Noto Sans SC Bold).

```bash
voiceover script examples/script.md -o out/          # audio only: out/voiceover.mp3 + .srt + manifest.json
voiceover say "Welcome back to the channel!" -o hello.mp3
voiceover doctor                                      # ffmpeg, engines, keys, fonts
```

No voices file is needed: every speaker in the script automatically gets its own voice, chosen from the script's language.

## What is AI Voiceover Studio?

AI Voiceover Studio is a free, MIT-licensed command-line tool and Python library for turning written scripts into narrated videos. You write narration in Markdown — optionally with speaker tags, pauses and one image or clip per paragraph — and the `voiceover` command produces the voiceover audio (MP3/WAV), SRT subtitles and an MP4 with B-roll, Ken Burns motion, transitions, word-by-word animated captions and background music ducked under the voice. It runs on your own machine with Python 3.9+ and ffmpeg, uses free Microsoft Edge neural voices by default (300+ voices, 70+ languages), and can switch to other text-to-speech engines such as OpenAI or Miragea (voice cloning) with one flag.

## Who is it for

- **Faceless YouTube channels** that publish narrated explainers, top-10s, history or science videos on a schedule.
- **Short-form creators** making vertical Shorts, Reels and TikToks with bold, word-by-word captions.
- **Educators and course authors** who want tutorials and lessons narrated from a script they can keep editing.
- **Localization and dubbing teams** producing the same video in several languages from translated scripts.
- **Podcasters and audiobook producers** who need scripted intros, trailers, ads and sample chapters.
- **Developers and AI agents** that generate narration or videos from code, in CI, or from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

## Why this exists

Most voiceover workflows for YouTube explainers, tutorials and faceless channels look the same: write a script, paste it paragraph by paragraph into a TTS tool, download a pile of clips, line them up in an editor, then transcribe everything again to get captions. AI Voiceover Studio does that whole loop from a plain Markdown file, reproducibly, so a script edit means re-running one command — and only the lines you changed are generated again.

## Features

| | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| 🆓 **Works without signup** | free Microsoft Edge neural voices via `edge-tts` are the default engine — 300+ voices, 70+ languages |
| 🎭 **Multi-speaker scripts** | `[NARRATOR]:` / `[ALEX]:` lines in Markdown or TXT; each speaker gets its own voice automatically, or map them in `voices.json` |
| 🎞️ **Faceless video** | B-roll per paragraph (`![](clip.mp4)` in the script) → MP4 with Ken Burns motion, slide / zoom / fade transitions, a light film grade and an animated hook card |
| 🔤 **Animated captions** | TikTok / CapCut-style word-by-word highlight from real word timings, pop-in, keyword colours (`**bold**` in the script), safe areas for 9:16 and 16:9 |
| 🎵 **Music with ducking** | built-in generated ambient tracks (no licence issues) or your own file, lowered automatically while the voice speaks |
| ✨ **No pictures? Still good** | parts without B-roll get an animated gradient with large kinetic typography of the key phrase |
| 💬 **Accurate subtitles** | SRT timed from the engine's own sentence boundaries, or speech recognition on the final mix; CJK-aware line wrapping |
| 🎨 **Caption styles** | `tiktok` (default for vertical), `clean` (default for landscape), `bold`, `minimal`, `box`; sizes adapt to 16:9 and 9:16 |
| 🧬 **Voice cloning** | with the Miragea engine: a reference audio URL (plus its transcript) instead of a stock voice |
| ♻️ **Re-run safely** | per-line cache and deterministic idempotency keys: unchanged lines are never generated twice |
| 🔌 **Pluggable engines** | `edge`, `miragea`, `openai`, offline `dummy`, or your own via a small `VoiceProvider` interface |
| 🩺 **`voiceover doctor`** | checks ffmpeg (libass), engines, API keys and CJK fonts, and tells you the exact fix |
| 🤖 **Agent-ready** | an agent skill plus `--json` output and stable exit codes for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and scripts |
| 🪶 **Tiny core** | standard library only; engines are optional extras; video is rendered by ffmpeg directly |

## Voice engines

| Engine | Setup | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `edge` *(default without a key)* | `pip install -e ".[edge]"` — no account, no key | trying it out, drafts, many languages |
| `miragea` *(default when `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` is set)* | `export MIRAGEA_API_KEY=...` ([create a key](https://miragea.ai/workspace/api)) | voice cloning from a reference clip, expressive models with emotion tags, subtitle recognition |
| `openai` | `export OPENAI_API_KEY=...` | OpenAI voices (`alloy`, `nova`, `onyx`, ...) |
| `dummy` | nothing (`--dry-run`) | offline tests and CI: silent audio with realistic timing |

Pick one with `--provider NAME` or `VOICEOVER_PROVIDER=NAME`. List voices with `voiceover voices --provider edge --filter en-GB` (Edge voice ids look like `en-GB-SoniaNeural`) or `voiceover voices` for the actors saved in your Miragea account.

Edge voices come from Microsoft's online read-aloud service through the community `edge-tts` package; they need an internet connection and are subject to Microsoft's terms. If you are behind an HTTPS proxy that edge-tts cannot use, set `VOICEOVER_EDGE_PROXY`.

## Multi-character scripts (dialogue and dubbing)

Write the script the way you would read it:

```markdown
# Why the Sky Is Blue — 60-second explainer

[NARRATOR]: Look up on a clear day and the sky is blue. But sunlight is white.
So where does the blue come from?

[ALEX](tags=curious): Wait — sunlight is white? It looks yellow to me.

[pause 0.8]

[ALEX](speed=1.05): So blue light bounces all over the sky!
```

Rules: a `[NAME]:` tag sets the speaker; untagged lines continue with the current speaker; a blank line starts a new segment; `[pause 1.5]` inserts silence; `(tags=a|b, speed=1.1, model=..., lang=...)` sets per-line options. Headings, HTML comments, code blocks and tables are skipped, and Markdown emphasis and links are read as plain text. Long paragraphs are split at sentence boundaries to stay within the engine's per-request text limit.

Without a voices file each speaker gets a distinct voice for the script's language (for example Andrew and Ava for English, Yunxi and Xiaoxiao for Chinese). To choose voices yourself, map speakers in `voices.json` (see [examples/voices.example.json](examples/voices.example.json)):

```json
{
  "NARRATOR": { "actor_id": "en-GB-RyanNeural" },
  "ALEX":     { "actor_id": "en-US-AvaNeural", "speed": 1.05 }
}
```

With Miragea, `actor_id` is an actor from `voiceover voices`, or use `reference_audio_url` + `reference_text` to clone a voice:

```json
{
  "NARRATOR": { "actor_id": "YOUR_ACTOR_ID", "model": "standard" },
  "ALEX":     { "reference_audio_url": "https://example.com/alex.wav",
                "reference_text": "The exact words spoken in alex.wav." }
}
```

```bash
voiceover script examples/script.md --voices voices.json -o out/ --gap 0.4
```

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `out/voiceover.mp3` | the full track (`--name voiceover.wav` for WAV) |
| `out/voiceover.srt` | subtitles aligned to the track |
| `out/segments/*.wav` | one clip per segment — also the cache for the next run |
| `out/manifest.json` | speakers, voices, text, start/end times and sentence timings per segment |

Edit one line and run again: only that line is regenerated. Use `--fresh` for a new take of everything.

## Voice cloning from a reference clip

Voice cloning uses the Miragea engine:

```bash
export MIRAGEA_API_KEY=...
voiceover say "This is my own voice, generated from text." \
  --voice https://example.com/my-voice.wav \
  --ref-text "The exact words I said in my-voice.wav." \
  --lang en -o cloned.mp3
```

A `--voice` value that starts with `http(s)://` is treated as reference audio; anything else is a voice id. The URL must be reachable by the API server. Providing the exact transcript (`--ref-text`) gives the engine the most accurate reference. Only clone voices you own or have explicit permission to use.

## Subtitles (SRT) for YouTube

| Mode | How | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--subtitles timing` *(default)* | Cues from the engine's sentence boundaries (edge) or from each segment's duration, text taken from the script | Your script is the source of truth — no extra call, no recognition errors |
| `--subtitles recognize` | Uploads the final mix to the engine's subtitle recognition (Miragea) | You want timing that follows the actual speech of any engine's audio |
| `--subtitles none` | No SRT | Audio-only projects |

Cues are split at sentence and clause boundaries, never overlap, and are wrapped to two balanced lines (CJK-aware). Upload the `.srt` to YouTube Studio → *Subtitles*, or burn it into the video (next section).

## Faceless YouTube video and Shorts from a script

Put the B-roll right in the script. A Markdown image line sets the picture or clip for the paragraph below it, and `**bold**` marks the words to highlight:

```markdown
# Cleopatra vs. the Moon landing

![](broll/en/01-pyramid.jpg)
Cleopatra lived closer to the **Moon landing** than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

![](broll/en/02-build.jpg)
The pyramid at Giza was finished around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born about **2,500 years** later.
```

```bash
voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok --music ambient -o video.mp4      # 16:9 YouTube
voiceover video --script examples/demo.zh.md --vertical --music ambient -o short.mp4          # 9:16 Short / Reel / TikTok
voiceover video --script notes.md -o explainer.mp4                                            # no pictures: kinetic typography
voiceover video --images slides/ --script script.md --music song.mp3 --music-volume 0.4 -o video.mp4
```

What happens: each paragraph is voiced; its B-roll is shown exactly while it is spoken (several images in one paragraph share its time; video clips are trimmed or looped). Stills get a slow push-in, pull-out or pan, shots change with a mix of slide, zoom and fade transitions, and a gentle contrast / vignette / grain grade makes generated or stock images sit together. The script's `# heading` becomes an animated hook card for the first two seconds. Captions follow the voice word by word using the engine's word timings (edge), or a reading-speed estimate for other engines.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `![](file)` in the script | — | B-roll (image or video clip) for that paragraph; paths are relative to the script |
| `--images DIR` | — | images / clips for paragraphs without `![](...)`, in file-name order |
| `--style tiktok\|clean\|bold\|minimal\|box` | `tiktok` vertical, `clean` landscape | `tiktok`: 1–4 big words, spoken word pops in yellow, keywords green · `bold`: huge words revealed as spoken · `clean`: calm two-line captions with a soft highlight · `minimal` / `box`: static lines |
| `--music ambient\|pulse\|FILE` | none | background music; `ambient` and `pulse` are generated by this project at render time (royalty-free), or any audio file (looped) |
| `--music-volume 0-1` | `0.5` | music level after loudness levelling |
| `--no-duck` | ducking on | keep the music level constant instead of lowering it under the voice |
| `--hook TEXT` / `--no-hook` | script's first `#` heading | animated hook card for the first `--hook-seconds` (2.2) |
| `--vertical` / `--size WxH` | `1920x1080` | `--vertical` = `1080x1920`; captions keep clear of the TikTok / Shorts buttons |
| `--transition-style mix\|fade\|slide\|zoom\|cut` | `mix` | transition look; `--transition SEC` sets the length (0.5) |
| `--grade cinematic\|none` | `cinematic` | contrast, vignette and film grain |
| `--motion kenburns\|none` | `kenburns` | motion on stills |
| `--fit cover\|contain` | `cover` | crop to fill, or fit onto a blurred copy of the image |
| `--font NAME\|FILE` | Inter, falling back to system fonts | caption font, e.g. a bold `.ttf`; for Chinese/Japanese make sure a CJK font is installed (`voiceover doctor` checks) |
| `--subtitles burn\|sidecar\|none` | `burn` | burn captions in (an `.srt` is written too), sidecar only, or none |
| `--speaker-labels` | off | speaker name above each caption (`minimal` / `box` styles) |
| `--no-progress-bar` | bar on | thin progress line at the bottom |

Without any pictures the video is not an empty gradient: each paragraph gets an animated colour field with its key phrase (the first `**bold**` phrase, or the strongest words of its first sentence) building up in large type.

Everything is rendered by one ffmpeg call (zoompan, xfade, libass, sidechaincompress), so there is no Python video dependency; the 34-second 1080p demo renders in about 80 seconds on two CPU cores. The demo B-roll in [`examples/broll`](examples/broll) was generated for this project and is free to reuse under the repository licence.

## Use it from Python

```python
from voiceover_studio import Studio

studio = Studio()                                    # edge, or miragea when MIRAGEA_API_KEY is set
studio.say("Hello!", None, "hello.mp3")              # voice picked from the text's language
studio.say("Hello!", "en-GB-SoniaNeural", "sonia.mp3", speed=1.1)

result = studio.render_script("script.md", "out/")   # one voice per speaker, automatically
print(result.audio_path, result.srt_path, round(result.duration, 1))
for seg in result.segments:
    print(seg.start, seg.end, seg.speaker, seg.voice, seg.text)

from voiceover_studio.video import render_video
render_video(studio, None, "examples/demo.en.md", "video.mp4", style="tiktok", music="ambient")
render_video(studio, None, "examples/demo.zh.md", "short.mp4", size=(1080, 1920))   # 9:16, tiktok captions

Studio("dummy").render_script("script.md", "dry/")   # offline, for tests and CI
```

Errors are typed: `ConfigError` (bad input), `ProviderError` (HTTP/API error with `.status`, `.code`, `.retryable`, `.task_id`, `.hint`), `TaskFailed` (the job finished as failed), `NotSupported` (the engine lacks a capability, e.g. cloning on edge).

## Use it from an AI coding agent

[`skills/ai-voiceover/SKILL.md`](skills/ai-voiceover/SKILL.md) is a drop-in skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar agents. Copy the folder into your agent's skills directory (for example `~/.claude/skills/` or `.cursor/skills/`), or point the agent at it, then ask: *"Voice `script.md` and make a captioned video from the images in `slides/`."* Every command supports `--json` and stable exit codes (`0` ok, `1` task failed, `2` usage/API error).

## Architecture

```
script.md ──► script.py ──► [Segment(speaker, text, options, pause)]
                                  │   voices.json ─► config.py (speaker → Voice), else provider.auto_voice()
                                  ▼
                            studio.py ── cache hit? ──► segments/NNN_speaker_hash.wav (+ .timing.json)
                                  │ no
                                  ▼
                     providers/base.py  VoiceProvider.synthesize()
                     ├─ providers/edge.py     edge-tts stream → audio + sentence boundaries
                     ├─ providers/miragea.py  POST /audio/generations → poll /tasks/{id} → download
                     ├─ providers/openai.py   POST /audio/speech
                     ├─ providers/dummy.py    offline silence with estimated duration
                     └─ your provider         (entry point "ai_voiceover_studio.providers")
                                  ▼
                       audio.py  decode → concat with gaps → export (wav / ffmpeg)
                                  ▼
                    subtitles.py  sentence/segment timing  or  provider.transcribe() → SRT
                                  ▼
            words.py  engine word boundaries (or estimate) → caption pages
                                  ▼
   captions.py + music.py + video.py  ASS (karaoke, hook, kinetic) → one ffmpeg graph:
                                      B-roll + Ken Burns + xfade + grade + captions + ducked music → MP4
```

Reliability details for remote engines:

- **Asynchronous tasks (Miragea).** Jobs are created, then polled using the server's `poll_after_seconds`; a wait timeout reports the task id so you can resume with `voiceover task <id> --wait` instead of submitting again.
- **Idempotency.** Every create request carries an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the exact request content. Retrying after a network error or re-running the script returns the original task rather than creating a duplicate.
- **Retries** happen only for errors the API marks `retryable` (and network failures), always with the same key.
- **Clear errors** for 401 (key rejected), 403 (no API access), 409 (key reused with different input), 413 (upload too large) and 429 (quota or rate limit), each with a one-line hint. Keys are never printed or written to `manifest.json`.

### Adding a voice engine

```python
from voiceover_studio.providers.base import VoiceProvider, SynthesisResult, Voice

class MyProvider(VoiceProvider):
    name = "myengine"
    max_text_length = 2000
    supports_auto_voices = True

    def synthesize(self, text, voice, *, audio_format="wav", cache_key=None):
        audio = call_my_engine(text, voice.actor_id, speed=voice.speed or 1.0)
        return SynthesisResult(audio=audio, format="wav")

    def auto_voice(self, n, language):          # optional: voice for the n-th speaker
        return Voice(actor_id=["voice-a", "voice-b"][n % 2])
```

Register it in your package's `pyproject.toml` and use `voiceover --provider myengine ...`:

```toml
[project.entry-points."ai_voiceover_studio.providers"]
myengine = "my_package.provider:MyProvider"
```

`list_voices()` and `transcribe()` are optional; return `meta={"words": [...]}` (or `"sentences"`) from `synthesize()` — items with `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text` — to get exactly timed word-by-word captions.

## Supported languages

- **edge**: 70+ languages and locales (`voiceover voices --provider edge`); automatic voices for English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Russian, picked from the script's text or `--lang`.
- **miragea**: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian, including voice cloning.
- Subtitle wrapping handles both space-separated and CJK text.

## How it compares

A neutral comparison with the two most common ways to make a narrated, captioned video. "Typical" describes the category in general, not any specific product.

| | Manual workflow in a video editor (e.g. CapCut) | Hosted AI video generators (SaaS, in general) | Calling a TTS API with your own code | **AI Voiceover Studio** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | timeline: paste text, drag clips by hand | web form or prompt | your code | a Markdown script (works with git) |
| Where it runs | desktop / mobile app | the vendor's cloud | wherever your code runs | your machine (Python + ffmpeg); text goes only to the voice engine you pick |
| Source code / licence | closed source | typically closed source, account required | depends on the API | open source, MIT |
| Change one line of the script | edit and re-time by hand | regenerate in the web app | your own caching logic | re-run one command; only changed lines are regenerated |
| Word-by-word captions | auto captions available, styled per project | varies by product | separate step | built in, timed from the engine's word boundaries |
| Multi-speaker scripts | one voice track at a time | varies by product | your own code | `[NAME]:` tags, one voice per speaker automatically |
| Batch, CI and AI agents | no | API on some products | yes | CLI with `--json`, Python API, agent skill |
| Voice engines | the app's voices | the vendor's voices | one API | free Edge voices, OpenAI, Miragea (cloning), or your own provider |
| Timeline editing, templates, stock library | ✅ full editor | ✅ typically included | — | ❌ not included: bring your own B-roll, or use kinetic typography |

If you need a full timeline editor or lip-sync, use an editor alongside this tool — it intentionally does one job well: script in; voiceover, captions and a clean video out.

## FAQ

More answers in [docs/FAQ.md](docs/FAQ.md).

**Do I need an API key?**
No. The default `edge` engine uses free online neural voices with no account. `--dry-run` works fully offline with silent audio. A Miragea key adds voice cloning and expressive voices; an OpenAI key adds OpenAI voices.

**How do I add AI voiceover to a YouTube video?**
Write your narration in a Markdown file, run `voiceover script script.md -o out/`, then drop `out/voiceover.mp3` onto your editor's timeline and upload `out/voiceover.srt` as YouTube subtitles. For a captioned video with no editing at all, add `![](image.jpg)` lines to the script and run `voiceover video --script script.md --music ambient -o video.mp4`.

**Can I make vertical Shorts / Reels?**
Yes: `--vertical`. Captions switch to the word-by-word `tiktok` style, get larger, and stay above the area the apps cover with buttons.

**Is the background music safe to use?**
The built-in `ambient` and `pulse` tracks are synthesized by ffmpeg from this project's own code at render time, so there is no third-party recording or licence involved. Your own file is your responsibility.

**Can I clone my own voice?**
Yes, with the Miragea engine: pass a URL of a short, clean recording as `--voice https://.../me.wav` and its exact transcript as `--ref-text`. Only clone voices you have the right to use.

**Can different characters have different voices?**
Yes — tag lines with `[NAME]:`. Each name gets its own voice automatically, or map names to voices in `voices.json`.

**Will re-running a script generate everything again?**
No. Each segment is cached by its text and voice settings, and remote requests use deterministic idempotency keys. Pass `--fresh` for a brand-new take.

**Something doesn't work — where do I start?**
Run `voiceover doctor` (add `--online` to synthesize one test line). It checks Python, ffmpeg with libass, installed engines, keys and CJK fonts, and prints the fix for each problem.

## Roadmap

- [x] Demo GIF and sample videos
- [x] Free default engine (edge) and OpenAI engine
- [x] Ken Burns motion, cross-fades and caption style presets
- [x] `voiceover doctor`
- [x] Inline B-roll in the script (`![](clip.mp4)`) timed to each paragraph
- [x] Background music with automatic ducking (built-in generated tracks)
- [x] Word-by-word (karaoke) animated captions, hook card, kinetic typography
- [ ] Stock-footage search for B-roll by keyword
- [ ] Translate-and-dub: script → other languages → voiceover
- [ ] Parallel segment generation with a concurrency limit
- [ ] Publish to PyPI

Ideas and votes welcome in [Issues](https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio/issues).

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome — bug reports, docs, new providers and features alike. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). In short:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,edge,yaml]"
pytest                      # fully offline: engines and HTTP are mocked, no key needed
```

Keep the core dependency-free, add tests with mocked network calls, and never commit keys or generated media (except the curated demo files in `docs/assets/`). Please follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and report security issues as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

If you use AI Voiceover Studio in research or a publication, cite it with [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) (GitHub's *Cite this repository* button).

# AI Voiceover Studio — FAQ

Answers about making AI voiceovers, text-to-speech videos, faceless YouTube videos and word-by-word captions with [AI Voiceover Studio](https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio), an open-source Python CLI. Every answer stands on its own and includes a command you can copy. Setup for all commands:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"     # Python 3.9+; video also needs ffmpeg
```

## Top questions

### How do I make a faceless YouTube video with AI for free?
Use AI Voiceover Studio, a free open-source Python CLI: write your narration in a Markdown file with an image or clip above each paragraph (`![](shot.jpg)`) and run `voiceover video --script script.md --music ambient -o video.mp4`. It voices the script with free Microsoft Edge neural voices (no account, no API key), shows each picture while its paragraph is spoken with Ken Burns motion, and burns in word-by-word captions and ducked background music. Try it on the bundled example: `voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok --music ambient -o out/video.mp4`. Guide: [faceless YouTube](use-cases/faceless-youtube.md).

### How do I add word-by-word captions to a video with Python?
AI Voiceover Studio generates TikTok-style word-by-word captions from a script: the voice engine reports when each word is spoken and the captions are rendered as animated ASS subtitles and burned in with ffmpeg. Run `voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok -o out/captions.mp4`, or from Python: `from voiceover_studio import Studio; from voiceover_studio.video import render_video; render_video(Studio(), None, "script.md", "out.mp4", style="tiktok")`. An `.srt` file is written next to the MP4 as well. It captions narration it generates itself; it does not transcribe an existing video's audio.

### What is the best open-source text to speech for YouTube videos?
It depends on whether you need offline voices, voice cloning or the least setup. AI Voiceover Studio (MIT) is an open-source tool around text-to-speech engines rather than a speech model itself: by default it uses free Microsoft Edge neural voices (300+ voices, 70+ languages, internet required), and it can switch to OpenAI or Miragea (voice cloning) with `--provider`. Fully offline open-source models can be added as a custom engine through its small `VoiceProvider` interface. To hear the default engine: `voiceover say "Welcome back to the channel!" -o hello.mp3`.

### How do I turn a script into a video automatically?
Run `voiceover video --script script.md -o video.mp4` with AI Voiceover Studio. Each paragraph of the Markdown script is voiced, shown with its own image or clip (`![](file)` above the paragraph) or, without pictures, with animated kinetic typography, and captioned word by word; the script's first `# heading` becomes an animated hook card. Example: `voiceover video --script examples/script.md -o out/explainer.mp4`.

### How do I make TikTok-style animated captions for free?
AI Voiceover Studio's `tiktok` caption style shows 1–4 big words at a time, pops the spoken word in yellow and colours keywords (marked `**bold**` in the script) green, and it is the default for vertical video. Run `voiceover video --script examples/demo.zh.md --vertical --music ambient -o out/short.mp4`. Other styles: `bold`, `clean`, `minimal`, `box`. It is free and open source (MIT) and needs ffmpeg with libass.

### How do I make YouTube Shorts, Reels or TikToks with an AI voiceover?
Add `--vertical` to AI Voiceover Studio's video command: `voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --vertical --music pulse -o out/short.mp4`. The video is rendered at 1080×1920 with large word-by-word captions kept clear of the buttons the apps overlay. Guide: [Shorts / Reels / TikTok](use-cases/shorts-reels-tiktok.md).

### How do I convert text to speech in Python and get an SRT subtitle file?
With AI Voiceover Studio, `voiceover script script.md -o out/` writes `out/voiceover.mp3`, a matching `out/voiceover.srt` and a `manifest.json` with per-line timings; subtitle timing comes from the engine's own sentence boundaries, so the text matches your script exactly. In Python: `from voiceover_studio import Studio; Studio().render_script("script.md", "out/")`. For a single line: `voiceover say "Hello world" -o hello.mp3`.

### How do I make a multi-voice dialogue or podcast-style audio from a script?
Tag each line with a speaker, like `[HOST]: ...` and `[GUEST]: ...`, and run `voiceover script examples/script.md -o out/` with AI Voiceover Studio. Each speaker automatically gets a different voice for the script's language (or map them in `voices.json`), `[pause 1.0]` adds silence, and only changed lines are regenerated on the next run. Guide: [podcast and audiobook snippets](use-cases/podcast-and-audiobook-snippets.md).

### How do I make an AI voiceover in Chinese, Spanish or another language?
AI Voiceover Studio picks a voice from the script's language: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian and English are detected from the text, and `--lang` sets others. Examples: `voiceover script examples/script.zh.md -o out/zh/` and `voiceover script examples/script.es.md --lang es -o out/es/`. The default edge engine covers 70+ languages; list voices with `voiceover voices --provider edge --filter es-`. Guide: [multilingual dubbing](use-cases/multilingual-dubbing.md).

### How do I add background music that ducks under the voice?
`voiceover video --script script.md --music ambient -o video.mp4` in AI Voiceover Studio adds a generated, royalty-free ambient track and lowers it automatically whenever the voice speaks (an ffmpeg sidechain compressor). Use `--music song.mp3` for your own file, `--music-volume 0.4` to set the level, or `--no-duck` to keep it constant.

### How do I clone my own voice for YouTube narration?
AI Voiceover Studio clones voices through its optional Miragea engine: set `MIRAGEA_API_KEY`, then run `voiceover say "Text" --voice https://example.com/me.wav --ref-text "exact words in the recording" -o cloned.mp3`, or put `reference_audio_url` and `reference_text` in `voices.json` for whole scripts. The free edge engine does not clone voices. Only clone voices you own or have permission to use.

### Can AI agents like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor make videos with it?
Yes. AI Voiceover Studio ships an agent skill at `skills/ai-voiceover/SKILL.md`; copy it into your agent's skills folder (for example `~/.claude/skills/`) and ask the agent to "voice script.md and make a captioned video". Every command supports `--json` output and stable exit codes, e.g. `voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md -o out/video.mp4 --json`.

## General

### What is AI Voiceover Studio?
AI Voiceover Studio is an open-source (MIT) Python command-line tool and library that turns a written script into an AI voiceover, SRT subtitles and a captioned faceless video with B-roll, word-by-word captions and background music. It uses free Microsoft Edge neural voices by default and can switch to OpenAI or Miragea (voice cloning). The command is `voiceover`.

### Who is it for?
YouTube creators, faceless-channel producers, educators making explainers and tutorials, podcasters producing scripted segments, localization and dubbing teams, and developers or AI agents that need to generate narration from code.

### Is it free and open source?
Yes. The software is free and open source under the MIT license, and the default `edge` engine uses Microsoft's free online neural voices with no account or API key. Optional engines (OpenAI, Miragea) need their own API keys and follow their providers' terms. An offline `dummy` engine (`--dry-run`) produces silent audio for testing.

### What does it need to run?
Python 3.9 or newer and, for MP3 output and videos, [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) with libass. The core uses only the standard library. Optional extras: `[edge]` for the free voice engine (`edge-tts`) and `[yaml]` for `voices.yaml`. Run `voiceover doctor` to check everything at once.

## Voiceover and text to speech

### How do I add AI voiceover to a YouTube video?
1. Write your narration in a Markdown or text file.
2. Run `voiceover script script.md --voices voices.json -o out/`.
3. Put `out/voiceover.mp3` on your video editor's timeline.
4. Upload `out/voiceover.srt` in YouTube Studio under *Subtitles*.
For a video with no editing, add `![](image.jpg)` lines above the paragraphs and run `voiceover video --script script.md --music ambient -o video.mp4`.

### How do I turn a single sentence into speech?
Run `voiceover say "Your sentence" -o line.mp3`. A voice is picked from the language of the text; choose one with `--voice`, e.g. `--voice en-GB-SoniaNeural` (list them with `voiceover voices --provider edge --filter en-GB`) or a Miragea actor id from `voiceover voices`.

### Can different characters have different voices?
Yes. Start lines with `[NAME]:` in the script. With the edge engine each name automatically gets its own voice for the script's language; to choose voices yourself, map names in `voices.json` or pass `--default-voice`. Lines without a tag continue with the previous speaker. With engines that have no automatic voices, a missing voice is reported before anything is generated.

### Can I control speed, emotion or style?
Yes. Use `--speed` (0.25–4) and `--tag` on the command line, or per line in the script: `[ALEX](tags=excited, speed=1.1): ...`. Available tags depend on the engine and model.

### How do I add pauses?
Put `[pause 1.5]` on its own line for 1.5 seconds of silence. `--gap` sets the default silence between segments (0.35 s).

### How long can a script be?
There is no fixed limit in the tool. Long paragraphs are split at sentence boundaries so that each request stays within the engine's per-request text limit, and the pieces are joined seamlessly.

### Does re-running a script generate everything again?
No. Every segment is cached by its exact text and voice settings in `out/segments/`, and remote requests use deterministic idempotency keys, so unchanged lines are reused. Use `--fresh` to force a new take.

## Voice cloning

### Why should I pass the reference transcript?
The transcript (`--ref-text` / `reference_text`) tells the engine exactly what is said in the reference clip, which gives the most accurate clone. If you leave it out, the engine recognizes the reference speech automatically.

### Is voice cloning legal?
Cloning your own voice, or a voice you have explicit written permission to use, is generally fine. Cloning someone else's voice without consent may violate their rights and the engine's terms. Do not use cloned voices to impersonate or deceive.

## Languages

### Which languages are supported?
The default `edge` engine offers 300+ voices in 70+ languages and locales (`voiceover voices --provider edge`). Voices are picked automatically from the text for English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Russian; for Spanish, French, German, Italian or Portuguese pass `--lang es` (etc.). The Miragea engine supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian, including voice cloning.

### Can I mix languages in one script?
Yes. Each segment is generated separately, so different lines can be in different languages or use different voices. Use `lang=` per line or `--lang` as a hint for reference audio.

### Does it work for dubbing a video into another language?
Yes, if you have the translated script: keep the same speaker tags and image lines, then run `voiceover script examples/script.es.md --lang es -o out/es/` (or `voiceover video ...`). See [multilingual dubbing](use-cases/multilingual-dubbing.md). Automatic translation is on the roadmap.

## Subtitles

### How are subtitles created?
By default (`--subtitles timing`) cues come from the sentence boundaries the engine reports while speaking (edge) or from the measured duration of each segment, with the text taken from your script, so there are no recognition errors and no extra API call. Cues never overlap. With `--subtitles recognize` (Miragea), the finished track is sent to the subtitle recognition endpoint for timing that follows the actual speech.

### What subtitle format is produced?
SRT, which YouTube, most video editors and players accept. Cues are split at sentence and clause boundaries and wrapped to at most two lines, with CJK-aware line breaking.

### Can subtitles be burned into the video?
Yes, and it is the default for `voiceover video`: captions are burned in with a style preset (`--style tiktok|clean|bold|minimal|box`; the animated styles highlight each word as it is spoken) and an `.srt` is written next to the MP4 as well. This needs ffmpeg with libass. Use `--subtitles sidecar` for the `.srt` only. Chinese, Japanese and Korean captions need a CJK font installed (for example `fonts-noto-cjk`); `voiceover doctor` checks for one.

## Faceless videos

### How is each image timed?
B-roll written in the script follows its paragraph; several images in one paragraph share its time, and video clips are trimmed or looped. With only `--images`, each image follows one segment when the counts match, otherwise the audio length is divided evenly.

### What if I have no images at all?
Parts without a picture get an animated gradient with the paragraph's key phrase in large kinetic type (the first `**bold**` phrase, or the strongest words of its first sentence), so a plain script still gives a watchable video.

### How do the word-by-word captions work?
The edge engine reports when each word is spoken, and captions highlight words in that rhythm: `tiktok` pops the spoken word in yellow, `bold` reveals huge words one by one, `clean` softly highlights a calm two-line caption. For engines without word timings the timing is estimated from sentence or paragraph length. Words in `**bold**` and numbers get a keyword colour.

### Can I make vertical videos for Shorts, Reels or TikTok?
Yes: add `--vertical` (= `--size 1080x1920`). Captions switch to the `tiktok` style, get larger and stay above the area the apps cover with their buttons. `--fit cover` crops images to fill the frame; `--fit contain` places them on a blurred background.

### Can I turn off the motion, transitions or effects?
Yes: `--motion none` keeps images still, `--transition 0` or `--transition-style cut` uses hard cuts, `--grade none` removes vignette and grain, and `--no-progress-bar` and `--no-hook` remove the progress line and hook card.

## Engines, API and security

### Which TTS engines are supported?
Built in: `edge` (free Microsoft Edge neural voices through `edge-tts`, the default when no Miragea key is set), `miragea` (voice cloning, expressive models, subtitle recognition; the default when `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` is set), `openai` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) and `dummy` (offline, for tests and dry runs). Choose with `--provider` or `VOICEOVER_PROVIDER`. Any other engine can be added by implementing the small `VoiceProvider` interface and registering it under the `ai_voiceover_studio.providers` entry point.

### Is the edge engine really free? What are the limits?
It uses Microsoft's online read-aloud voices through the community `edge-tts` package, with no account or key. It needs an internet connection, does not support voice cloning, and its use is subject to Microsoft's terms. For cloning or expressive control use Miragea.

### edge-tts fails behind my proxy
Some HTTPS proxy URLs (for example ones with special characters in the user name) cannot be used by the underlying HTTP library. Set `VOICEOVER_EDGE_PROXY` to a usable proxy URL, or unset `HTTPS_PROXY` for the command. `voiceover doctor --online` tests a real synthesis.

### How do I get a Miragea API key?
Create one at https://miragea.ai/workspace/api and set it with `export MIRAGEA_API_KEY=...`. For a self-hosted deployment, also set `MIRAGEA_BASE_URL` (including `/v1`).

### Can I try it without an API key?
Yes. The default `edge` engine needs no key or account. `--dry-run` works fully offline: it writes silent audio with realistic durations, so you can check parsing, subtitles and video layout.

### What does `voiceover doctor` check?
Python version, ffmpeg and its libass/xfade filters, which engines are installed, whether `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` are set (values are never shown), which engine is the default, and whether a CJK caption font is installed. `--online` also synthesizes one short line with the edge engine. Each problem comes with the command that fixes it.

### Is my API key safe?
Keys are read only from environment variables (`MIRAGEA_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`), sent only in the `Authorization` header to the API host, never printed, logged or written to `manifest.json`, and not sent when downloading result files. Redirects are not followed for authenticated requests.

### What happens if the network drops or a job takes long?
Create requests carry an idempotency key, so retrying returns the original job instead of creating a duplicate. Tasks are polled until they finish; if the wait times out, the task id is reported and `voiceover task <id> --wait -o file.mp3` resumes it.

### What do the error codes mean?
`401` the key was rejected; `403` the account has no API access; `409` an idempotency key was reused with different input; `413` the upload is too large; `429` quota exhausted or rate limited. The CLI prints a one-line hint for each. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` task failed, `2` usage or API error.

# Make a faceless YouTube video with AI from a script

**Short answer:** with [AI Voiceover Studio](../../README.md) you write the narration in a Markdown file, put an image or clip above each paragraph, and run one command. You get a 1080p MP4 with an AI voiceover, B-roll with Ken Burns motion, word-by-word captions, an animated hook card and background music — using free neural voices, with no account or API key.

## Run it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --style tiktok --music ambient -o out/faceless.mp4
```

Output: `out/faceless.mp4` (1920×1080), `out/faceless.srt` (upload it to YouTube Studio → *Subtitles*), and the voiceover track in `out/faceless_voiceover/`. Needs Python 3.9+ and ffmpeg; run `voiceover doctor` if anything is missing. This is the command that produced the [16:9 demo](../assets/demo.mp4).

## Write your own script

```markdown
# Cleopatra vs. the Moon landing

![](broll/en/01-pyramid.jpg)
Cleopatra lived closer to the **Moon landing** than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

![](broll/en/02-build.jpg)
The pyramid at Giza was finished around 2560 BC. Cleopatra was born about **2,500 years** later.
```

- The `# heading` becomes the hook card shown in the first seconds (`--hook "..."` to override, `--no-hook` to remove).
- `![](file)` sets the picture or video clip for the paragraph below it; paths are relative to the script.
- `**bold**` words are highlighted in the captions.
- No pictures yet? Leave the image lines out and each paragraph gets animated kinetic typography instead.

## Useful options

| Goal | Option |
| --- | --- |
| Calm captions instead of big words | `--style clean` |
| Your own music, quieter | `--music song.mp3 --music-volume 0.35` |
| A specific voice | `--default-voice en-GB-RyanNeural` (list: `voiceover voices --provider edge --filter en-`) |
| Use a folder of images in name order | `--images my-broll/` |
| Matching font of the demo | `--font Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf` |
| Preview offline, no voice service | `--dry-run` |

Related: [Shorts / Reels / TikTok](shorts-reels-tiktok.md) · [FAQ](../FAQ.md)

# Make YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikToks with word-by-word captions

**Short answer:** add `--vertical` to the `voiceover video` command of [AI Voiceover Studio](../../README.md). The video is rendered at 1080×1920, captions switch to the TikTok-style word-by-word preset (1–4 big words, the spoken word pops in yellow, keywords in green), and they stay above the area the apps cover with buttons.

## Run it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover video --script examples/demo.zh.md --vertical --music ambient -o out/short.mp4
```

This is the command that produced the [9:16 Chinese demo](../assets/demo-short-zh.mp4). For an English Short from the same kind of script:

```bash
voiceover video --script examples/demo.en.md --vertical --music pulse -o out/short-en.mp4
```

Chinese, Japanese and Korean captions need a CJK font (for example `fonts-noto-cjk`); `voiceover doctor` checks for one, and `--font NotoSansSC-Bold.otf` picks a specific file.

## Tips for short-form

- Keep it under 60 seconds: roughly 130–160 English words or 250–300 Chinese characters.
- Put the hook in the `# heading`; it is shown as an animated card for the first 2.2 s (`--hook-seconds` to change).
- Mark one or two keywords per paragraph with `**bold**` so they light up in the captions.
- `--fit contain` keeps landscape images whole on a blurred background instead of cropping them.
- `--style bold` reveals huge words one by one; `--style clean` gives calmer two-line captions.

Related: [Faceless YouTube](faceless-youtube.md) · [Multilingual dubbing](multilingual-dubbing.md) · [FAQ](../FAQ.md)

# Narrate explainers, tutorials and movie recaps with AI voiceover

**Short answer:** [AI Voiceover Studio](../../README.md) voices your script paragraph by paragraph and shows each image, slide or video clip exactly while its paragraph is spoken. Put a folder of slides or clips next to a narration script and one command gives you a narrated, captioned MP4 plus the separate voiceover track and SRT for your editor.

## Run it

Narrate a folder of images or clips, used in file-name order, one per paragraph:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover video --script examples/script.md --images examples/broll/en --style clean -o out/explainer.mp4
```

`examples/script.md` is a two-voice science explainer (`[NARRATOR]` and `[ALEX]`); each speaker gets a different voice automatically.

## Movie and series recaps

Cut your scenes into short clips (`01.mp4`, `02.mp4`, …) and reference them in the script, one per paragraph:

```markdown
# The ending, explained

![](clips/01.mp4)
In the final scene, the detective finally realises the letters were never from her sister.

![](clips/02.mp4)
That changes **everything** we saw in the first episode.
```

```bash
voiceover video --script recap.md --style clean --transition-style cut --grade none -o recap.mp4
```

Clips are trimmed or looped to the length of their paragraph. Use only footage you have the right to use, and check the platform's rules on commentary and fair use.

## Audio only, for your own editor

```bash
voiceover script examples/script.md -o out/narration/
```

Gives `out/narration/voiceover.mp3`, `voiceover.srt` and a `manifest.json` with the start and end time of every paragraph, so you can line up cuts in Premiere, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut.

Related: [Faceless YouTube](faceless-youtube.md) · [Podcast and audiobook snippets](podcast-and-audiobook-snippets.md) · [FAQ](../FAQ.md)

# Multilingual dubbing: one video, several languages

**Short answer:** write (or translate) one script per language with the same speaker tags and image lines, then run [AI Voiceover Studio](../../README.md) once per script. Voices are picked automatically for each language — detected from the text for English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Russian, or set with `--lang` (for example `--lang es` gives Álvaro and Elvira) — so the same video comes out dubbed in every language with matching captions.

## Run it

The repository ships the same two-voice explainer in English, Chinese and Spanish:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover script examples/script.md    -o out/en/
voiceover script examples/script.zh.md -o out/zh/
voiceover script examples/script.es.md -o out/es/ --lang es
```

`--lang` is needed for Latin-script languages other than English (Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese), because the text alone does not tell them apart reliably. Each folder gets `voiceover.mp3` and `voiceover.srt` in that language. For finished videos with burned-in captions, use `voiceover video` the same way:

```bash
voiceover video --script examples/script.es.md --lang es --images examples/broll/en -o out/es.mp4
```

## Tips

- Keep the same paragraph order and `![](...)` lines in every language, so the pictures stay in sync.
- Choose voices per language with a voices file (`"NARRATOR": {"actor_id": "es-MX-JorgeNeural"}`); list them with `voiceover voices --provider edge --filter es-`.
- The free edge engine covers 70+ languages and locales. To keep the *same* voice across languages, use a cloned voice with the Miragea engine (`reference_audio_url` in `voices.json`).
- Translation is up to you (or your translation tool); automatic translate-and-dub is on the roadmap.

Related: [Shorts / Reels / TikTok](shorts-reels-tiktok.md) · [FAQ](../FAQ.md)


================================================================================
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio/main/docs/use-cases/podcast-and-audiobook-snippets.md
================================================================================

# Podcast intros, trailers and audiobook samples with multi-voice text to speech

**Short answer:** [AI Voiceover Studio](../../README.md) turns a tagged script into one mixed audio file with a different voice per character, controlled pauses and an SRT transcript. That makes it a quick way to produce podcast intros and outros, episode trailers, ad reads and audiobook sample chapters from text.

## Run it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yanghhu/ai-voiceover-studio && cd ai-voiceover-studio
pip install -e ".[edge]"
voiceover script examples/script.md --voices examples/voices.edge.json --gap 0.5 -o out/podcast/
```

Output: `out/podcast/voiceover.mp3`, `voiceover.srt` (a timed transcript), one clip per line in `segments/` and `manifest.json`. Use `--name episode-intro.wav` for uncompressed audio.

## Script format

```markdown
[HOST]: Welcome back to the show. Today: why the sky is blue.

[GUEST](tags=curious, speed=1.05): I always thought sunlight was yellow!

[pause 1.0]

[HOST]: Let's find out.
```

- Each `[NAME]:` gets its own voice automatically, or map names to voices in `voices.json`.
- `[pause 1.0]` inserts silence; `--gap` sets the default gap between lines.
- For audiobook narration, a slightly slower pace often sounds better: `--speed 0.95`.
- Re-running only regenerates lines you changed, so long chapters are cheap to revise.

## A single line

```bash
voiceover say "Thanks for listening — see you next week." -o outro.mp3
```

Use only voices you have the right to use; cloning (Miragea engine) requires the speaker's permission.

Related: [Explainer narration](explainer-and-recap-narration.md) · [FAQ](../FAQ.md)

---
name: ai-voiceover
description: Turn a written script into an AI voiceover (text to speech, multi-speaker, voice cloning) with SRT subtitles and optionally a captioned faceless video, using the `voiceover` CLI from ai-voiceover-studio. Works with free voices and no API key. Use when the user asks to voice, narrate, dub or add a voiceover/subtitles to a script or video.
---

# AI Voiceover

Use the `voiceover` CLI (package `ai-voiceover-studio`, Python 3.9+) to generate narration.

## Setup check

1. `voiceover --version` — if missing: `pip install -e "<repo>[edge]"`
   (`[edge]` = free voices, `[yaml]` = voices.yaml).
2. Run `voiceover doctor --json` and fix any `fail` it reports (it never prints keys).
3. Engines: without keys the free `edge` engine is used (internet needed, no account).
   `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` switches the default to Miragea (voice cloning, expressive models);
   `OPENAI_API_KEY` enables `--provider openai`. Never ask the user to paste a key into chat,
   never echo it, never write it to files.
4. MP3 output and video need `ffmpeg` (with libass for burned captions).

## Workflow: voice a script

1. **Prepare the script** (Markdown or TXT). One speaker tag per line or paragraph:
   ```
   [NARRATOR]: Opening line.
   Untagged lines continue the current speaker.

   [ALEX](tags=excited, speed=1.1): A different character.
   [pause 1]
   ```
   Headings, HTML comments, code blocks and tables are ignored.
2. **Voices (optional).** Without a voices file every speaker gets its own voice automatically,
   chosen from the script's language. To choose: `voiceover voices --json` (add
   `--provider edge --filter en-GB` for Edge voices such as `en-GB-SoniaNeural`; for Miragea
   `voice_id` = actor id). If two voices share a name, ask the user which one. With Miragea a
   voice can also be a public reference-audio URL plus its exact transcript (`reference_text`).
   Only clone voices the user owns or has permission to use.
3. **Write `voices.json`** if the user picked voices (upper-case keys):
   ```json
   {"NARRATOR": {"actor_id": "en-US-AndrewNeural"}, "ALEX": {"actor_id": "en-US-AvaNeural", "speed": 1.05}}
   ```
4. **Dry run** (offline, validates speakers and timing):
   `voiceover script script.md -o out/ --dry-run --json`
5. **Generate**: `voiceover script script.md [--voices voices.json] -o out/ --json`
   Outputs `out/voiceover.mp3`, `out/voiceover.srt`, `out/manifest.json`, `out/segments/`.
6. Report the saved paths and duration. Do not claim success unless the command exited 0.

## Other commands

- One line: `voiceover say "text" [--voice <voice id|https://ref.wav>] [--ref-text "..."] [--lang en] -o line.mp3`
- Faceless video: `voiceover video --script script.md -o video.mp4 [--vertical] [--style tiktok|clean|bold|minimal|box] [--music ambient|pulse|file] [--images dir/] [--font file.ttf] [--subtitles burn|sidecar|none]`
  Put `![](path/to/image-or-clip)` above a paragraph to show it while that paragraph is spoken
  (paths relative to the script); `**bold**` words are highlighted. Word-by-word captions are burned in
  by default; the first `# heading` becomes a hook card (`--hook`, `--no-hook`). Paragraphs without a
  picture get kinetic typography. `--music ambient` adds generated, royalty-free music ducked under
  the voice. For Shorts / Reels / TikTok use `--vertical`. For CJK captions pass a CJK `--font`.
- Subtitles from speech recognition instead of timing (Miragea): add `--subtitles recognize` (one extra API call).
- Resume a task after a wait timeout: `voiceover task <task_id> --wait -o out.mp3`.

## Rules

- Re-running the same command is safe: unchanged segments come from cache and remote
  requests reuse idempotency keys. Use `--fresh` only when the user wants a new take.
- On a wait timeout, keep the reported `task_id` and resume with `voiceover task`; do not resubmit.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 provider task failed, 2 usage/config/API error. With `--json`, errors are
  `{"error": {"code", "message", "http_status", "retryable"}, "task_id"?}`.
- 401: key rejected → user checks the key variable. 403: account lacks API access.
  429: quota/rate limit → wait, do not loop. 400: fix text/voice/speed/tags.
- `proxy_unsupported` (edge): set `VOICEOVER_EDGE_PROXY` or unset `HTTPS_PROXY` for the command.
- Languages: edge covers 75 languages; Miragea covers Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German,
  French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian (with voice cloning).

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- Use-case guides with runnable commands in `docs/use-cases/` (faceless YouTube, Shorts / Reels /
  TikTok, explainer and recap narration, multilingual dubbing, podcast and audiobook snippets).
- Spanish example script `examples/script.es.md`.
- `llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file, built by `scripts/build_llms_full.py`), `CITATION.cff`,
  Code of Conduct, security policy, issue and pull request templates, social preview image.

### Changed
- `--lang` now also chooses the automatic voices for a whole script (e.g. `--lang es` gives Spanish
  voices for every speaker); before, it was only a hint for reference audio.
- README (all languages): definition, who it is for, use cases and a neutral comparison table;
  FAQ reorganised around common questions; `llms.txt` follows the llmstxt.org format.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added
- **Word-by-word animated captions** (`--style tiktok`, the new default for vertical video): 1-4 big
  words at a time, thick outline, the spoken word pops in and turns yellow, keywords stay green. Also
  `bold` (huge words revealed as spoken) and an upgraded `clean` (calm two-line captions with a soft
  highlight, default for landscape). Timing comes from the edge engine's word boundaries
  (`meta["words"]`), or a reading-speed estimate for other engines. Safe areas for 9:16 and 16:9.
- **B-roll in the script**: `![](image-or-clip)` above a paragraph shows it while the paragraph is
  spoken; several images share the paragraph's time; video clips are trimmed or looped.
  `**bold**` words become caption keywords.
- **Background music with ducking**: `--music ambient|pulse` (generated by ffmpeg from this project's
  own code at render time, no licence involved) or `--music FILE`; levelled, faded, and lowered under
  the voice with a sidechain compressor (`--music-volume`, `--no-duck`).
- **Animated hook card** from the script's `# heading` (`--hook`, `--hook-seconds`, `--no-hook`).
- **Kinetic typography** for parts without a picture: animated gradient + the key phrase building up
  in large type.
- Transitions mix (`--transition-style mix|fade|slide|zoom|cut`), a light cinematic grade
  (`--grade cinematic|none`: contrast, vignette, grain), smoother Ken Burns (four moves on a
  supersampled canvas), `--vertical` shortcut.
- New demo: `examples/demo.en.md` (16:9) and `examples/demo.zh.md` (9:16) with generated B-roll in
  `examples/broll/`; new `docs/assets/demo.gif`, `demo-short-zh.gif`, `demo.mp4`, `demo-short-zh.mp4`.

### Changed
- `--title` is now the hook card (alias `--hook`) and is shown whenever the script has a heading.
- `--speed`, `--tag` and other CLI voice options now also apply to automatically picked voices.
- Fonts given as a file are matched by their real family name, so single-weight files
  (e.g. `Montserrat-ExtraBold.ttf`) work with libass.
- The video is encoded in a temporary folder and moved into place (fixes `+faststart` on some
  network / FUSE file systems).
- Removed the old clip-art example slides (`examples/slides`, `examples/make_slides.py`).

## [0.2.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added
- **Free `edge` engine** (Microsoft Edge neural voices via `edge-tts`, extra `[edge]`): no account or
  key; it is the default engine when `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` is not set. Sentence boundaries reported by the
  engine are used for subtitle timing; network errors are retried; clear message for unusable
  proxy URLs (`VOICEOVER_EDGE_PROXY`).
- **`openai` engine** (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, standard library HTTP, `tags` become a speaking-style instruction).
- **Automatic voices per speaker**: without a voices file every speaker gets its own voice, chosen from the
  script's language (edge, openai, dummy) or from the actors saved in the Miragea account.
- **New video renderer** built on a single ffmpeg graph: Ken Burns zoom/pan with easing, cross-fades
  (`--transition`), progress bar, title card from the script's first heading, gradient background when no
  images are given, `--fit contain` with a blurred backdrop.
- **Caption styles** (`--style clean|box|bold|minimal`), `--speaker-labels`, `--font`; caption size and
  line length adapt to landscape and vertical video; CJK-aware.
- **`voiceover doctor`** (`--online`, `--json`): checks Python, ffmpeg filters (libass, xfade), engines,
  API keys (never shown), default engine and CJK fonts, with a fix for each problem.
- `voiceover voices --filter TEXT`; `voiceover say` without `--voice` picks a voice from the text's language.
- Real demo media in `docs/assets/` (GIF, MP4, MP3, SRT, vertical Chinese Short) and redrawn example
  slides generated by `examples/make_slides.py`.

### Changed
- Default engine is resolved as: `--provider` / `VOICEOVER_PROVIDER`, else `miragea` when
  `MIRAGEA_API_KEY` is set, else `edge`.
- `voiceover video` burns styled captions by default (`--subtitles burn`) and still writes the `.srt`;
  `--images` is optional.
- Video no longer depends on moviepy; the `[video]` extra is kept (empty) for compatibility.
- Subtitle cues never overlap.
- Miragea requests send a browser-compatible User-Agent that still names the tool.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added
- `voiceover say`: text to speech for a single line, with actor ids or a reference-audio URL (voice cloning).
- `voiceover script`: multi-speaker Markdown/TXT scripts (`[SPEAKER]:` tags, `[pause N]`, per-line
  `tags`/`speed`/`model`/`lang`), speaker → voice mapping via `voices.json` / `voices.yaml`,
  concatenation with configurable gaps, `manifest.json`, and a per-segment cache.
- SRT subtitles from segment timing (default) or provider speech recognition (`--subtitles recognize`).
- `voiceover video`: faceless slideshow video (moviepy) with sidecar or burned-in subtitles,
  landscape or vertical sizes.
- `voiceover voices` (account voice list, pagination) and `voiceover task` (resume/inspect a task).
- Provider interface (`VoiceProvider`) with entry-point discovery; built-in `miragea` provider
  (async tasks, polling, deterministic idempotency keys, retry on retryable errors, clear
  401/403/409/413/429 messages) and offline `dummy` provider.
- Agent skill `skills/ai-voiceover/SKILL.md`, `--json` output and stable exit codes.
- Offline test-suite with mocked HTTP.
